Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

statement noun

something stated

also make a statement, a true statement, a false statement

classical

Cic. Off. 1.23: dictōrum conventōrumque cōnstantia et vēritās

dictum, dictī n.

noun, second declension

what someone has said, a statement

Latin often names a statement by what was said: quod dīcis, “what you say”.

Other words

  • affirmātiō, affirmātiōnis f. — an assertion, a solemn statement

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.104: est enim jūs jūrandum affirmātiō religiōsa

    Also spelled adfirmātiō.

  • prōnūntiātum, prōnūntiātī n. — a statement in logic, a proposition

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.14: id ergō est prōnūntiātum, quod est vērum aut falsum

    Cicero’s rendering of Greek ἀξίωμα, made up on the spot (“so it occurs to me to call it for now”); a term of philosophy.

Examples

  • id ergō est prōnūntiātum, quod est vērum aut falsum

    a statement, then, is whatever is either true or falseCic. Tusc. 1.14

  • est enim jūs jūrandum affirmātiō religiōsa

    for an oath is a statement made under religious sanctionCic. Off. 3.104

See also say, comment, claim.
